recovered_habits.boundary_condition: A cheaper option is acceptable when it does not create brittle timing, poor room setup, extra fatigue, or a bad recovery trade-off.
recovered_habits.default_action: Group options by what will actually work first, then show cheaper options only as context or backups.

evidence.quote: Can you help me build a practical flight-and-hotel shortlist, not just the cheapest?
I need drive-versus-fly by practicality, not just cheapest.
Can you compare flights and hotels by practicality, not just cheapest?
Can you build me a practical flight and hotel shortlist, not just the cheapest thing?
Start with the practical groupings, not cheapest-first.
I need the options grouped by what is actually workable, not just the cheapest.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If costs become meaningfully high, keep a budget fallback visible, but label the practical cost of using it.
recovered_habits.name: Rank travel options by practical fit before price
recovered_habits.preference_value: Practicality, schedule protection, fatigue management, and usable logistics outrank the lowest fare or room rate.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: When comparing flights, hotels, drive-versus-fly choices, or full trip packages for both work and recovery trips.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: One-stop flights are acceptable when the layover is not silly and the arrival still leaves a usable evening or setup window.
recovered_habits.default_action: Choose a nonstop or a connection with a sane buffer, even at higher cost, if it preserves setup time and sleep.

evidence.quote: The one-stop outbound is fine if the layover isn’t silly. And please grab window seats if selection is available.
Book the nonstop outbound. I don’t want the after-10 p.m. one-stop before an 8 a.m. workshop.
No late connection. Book the nonstops. Window seats if available.
Don’t keep dangling the cheap one if it sets up a bad Saturday. It sounds like a false economy.
That Atlanta one is too tight. Is the 11:18 nonstop reliable enough, or is morning safer because of January weather?
Morning outbound is early, but probably better than arriving at bedtime. Any hidden problem with the Monday 2:18?

recovered_habits.exception_condition: A cheap late/tight routing can remain as a backup only when setup becomes irrelevant or the host provides enough protection that arrival timing no longer drives the trip.
recovered_habits.name: Protect outbound setup and next-day teaching over cheap late routings
recovered_habits.preference_value: For outbound work travel, avoid late arrivals, tight connections, and cheap routings that jeopardize setup, walk-throughs, or early teaching readiness.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Outbound flights for clinic trainings, seminars, conferences, or any trip with a required setup window or early next-day start.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: A same-day return is acceptable when the end time is a real hard stop, teardown is light, and the home arrival is not punishing.
recovered_habits.default_action: Pick an afternoon or next-day return with enough time for teardown, packing, transport, and airport processing.

evidence.quote: Monday morning is a last resort. I teach at 10 a.m. Monday, so if I fly home late Sunday, it needs to not be a midnight arrival. The Sunday lab end time is the big unknown.
I don’t want an airport sprint.
Thursday morning. I don’t want a near-midnight landing with that kit.
Assume Sunday. I don’t want to sprint out of a gait lab with equipment half packed.
Sunday 1:42 is the one. If the hospital complains about another hotel night, I want the reason spelled out.
Yes. Group by practicality. I need a room that won't make mornings harder. Monday afternoon return unless there is a magically clean Sunday escape.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Use Monday, Thursday morning, or another next-day return when end times are vague, demo gear is involved, or a late arrival would damage the next day.
recovered_habits.name: Use return buffers rather than airport sprints
recovered_habits.preference_value: Avoid rushed post-lab departures and near-midnight returns; add a later return or extra night when teardown, debrief, gear, or next-day teaching makes same-day travel brittle.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Return planning after seminars, labs, debriefs, races, or recovery weekends, especially when a Monday or next-day work block follows.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Queen is sufficient; king is not required. Fancy lobby or charm is not a deciding factor.
recovered_habits.default_action: Choose the better-rated suite or predictable room setup even if it is farther from the venue or costs more.

evidence.quote: For hotels: I want something reliably rated, ideally 4.0+ from guest reviews. Queen bed is fine, but I need a coffee maker and mini-fridge. Pool/hot tub/gym would be good because Saturday is long, but location matters.
Room setup: one bed is fine. Queen is enough; king is not necessary. If the lodge only has doubles, skip it.
Use the comfortable one, not the midnight-ish one. And book the offsite suite. The fridge being just a request at the connected hotel is enough to push me away.
Can the suite confirm actual queen, coffee, and fridge? Not a request basis?
The guesthouse room details are what worry me. I cannot be guessing about coffee and a fridge before a lab weekend.
I don't need a lobby. The adjacent one being below 4-ish and fuzzy on the fridge makes me nervous before an early Wednesday.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: A less certain official/connected hotel can be accepted when proximity materially reduces lab-material movement or conference friction and the missing fridge can be handled with a backup.
recovered_habits.name: Hotel basics must be confirmed, not assumed
recovered_habits.preference_value: Prefer reliable, well-reviewed lodging with a real queen/king or queen studio, in-room coffee maker, and confirmed fridge/mini-fridge; avoid doubles, run-of-house bedding, unclear fridge, and borderline review patterns.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Hotel selection for work trips, conferences, and recovery weekends when sleep, breakfast routine, or teaching readiness matters.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: No hot tub can be acceptable when the room setup, location, or conference/lab logistics are stronger.
recovered_habits.default_action: Prefer properties with pool/hot tub/fitness when otherwise practical; verify hours, seasonal closures, and maintenance, and state missing recovery pieces plainly.

evidence.quote: Hotel base is the part I'm stuck on. Downtown sounds nicer for Sunday food, but after Bent Creek, hot tub may be more useful. I don't want a no-fridge surprise.
Call out the missing recovery pieces plainly. I don’t want to read between the lines.
For this one the hot tub matters if we hike two days. I do not want to pay resort prices though.
I don’t care enough about a hot tub to haul lab stuff back and forth. The mini-fridge is the sticking point.

We can do either Thursday after 4:30 or Friday morning. Monday afternoon is better than a late-night return. We want two hikes, probably one Blue Ridge Parkway day, and I do care about a hot tub or pool if the fees are not ridiculous.
I care about total cost with taxes, parking, and resort fees, beach access, recent reviews, cancellation, queen or king bed, coffee and fridge, and pool/hot tub/fitness. Not just cheapest.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: For recovery-focused leisure trips, pay somewhat more for hot tub/pool/fitness when fees are transparent and not ridiculous.
recovered_habits.name: Treat recovery amenities as valuable but secondary
recovered_habits.preference_value: Pool, hot tub, and fitness access are meaningful recovery amenities, especially after hiking or long teaching days, but they do not override confirmed room basics, key location logistics, or unreasonable fees.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Hotel and lodging comparisons where the trip includes hiking, biking, long lab days, or recovery time.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Do not pay silly or large fees just for a window or forward seat; small user-approved fees can be acceptable.
recovered_habits.default_action: Book regular/Main Cabin or equivalent when needed for seat selection; choose windows where available; for two-person trips keep seats together, ideally with the user at the window.

evidence.quote: A. Don’t pay extra just for the last window if it’s silly. What are the hotel caveats now?
For seats, adjacent matters more than window; if we can get window-aisle together, great, but don't split us.
For fares, don't use basic if seats are random. I need to pick now.
Use the paid return window if it stays under $30. No checked bag.
Skip basic.
Take the outbound window pairs. Return keep us adjacent and free. I do not care $136 worth after the resort fees.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If no free window is open, choose the best non-middle or adjacent option and set a seat alert or check-in reminder.
recovered_habits.name: Use fare classes and seat choices that preserve seat control
recovered_habits.preference_value: Avoid random-seat/basic fares when seat control matters; prefer window seats when traveling solo, but on partner trips adjacent seats matter more than a window.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Flight booking and seat selection for solo work travel and partner leisure travel.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Book when cancellation terms are acceptable and the remaining uncertainty is small or operationally manageable.
recovered_habits.default_action: Hold cancellable rooms early if inventory or block deadlines matter, watch rates, and wait to ticket flights until timing and logistics are confirmed.

evidence.quote: I’d like a refundable room until the program is final, and I’d prefer one queen if that’s selectable.
No airfare until we see the event packet.
No booking until they answer.
For now hold the suite if it has free cancellation. Don't book flights until Wednesday is settled.
Put the lead in the file but don’t book yet. I’ll ask the conference about the Wednesday check-in window and send one more note to the headquarters hotel.
Hold both then. No flights until we get the presenter check-in and teardown answers.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: If a hotel rate will flip or a block deadline is imminent, hold or book the flexible room but keep flights unbooked until the travel times are real.
recovered_habits.name: Hold flexible lodging and delay flights until schedule risks are known
recovered_habits.preference_value: Use refundable/cancellable lodging holds while programs, host details, or lab timing are unresolved; avoid locking flights until the critical schedule answers are in.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Trip planning when conference programs, host access, teardown, observation windows, or reimbursement approval are not final.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Rideshare is preferred for simple urban trips with manageable bags and host storage; rental is preferred for repeated suburban commutes, demo gear, grocery logistics, or trail access.
recovered_habits.default_action: Wait for host parking/storage/entrance details, then choose the least fussy transport mode; when renting, prefer compact or appropriately small vehicle, pay-later, no prepaid fuel.

evidence.quote: So no car unless the host can’t give me anything specific?
Let’s skip the rental. Set up the SUV option if they can handle one large roller and one duffel.
Book the compact rental. Avoid prepaid fuel.
Book the compact, not prepaid. No giant SUV substitution if they ask.
Book the compact car too. I don't want to wait on rideshares with the props.
My partner can make Thursday work. If the fare is still close, go ahead with the GSP plan, the lodge, and the small SUV. But tell me the seat situation before you book.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Use a scheduled/local SUV or XL rideshare instead of a rental when the main problem is a one-time gear drop and parking would be more annoying than useful.
recovered_habits.name: Choose ground transport based on gear, timing, and parking rather than habitually renting
recovered_habits.preference_value: Do not rent by default; use rideshare or scheduled SUV when it avoids parking friction, but rent a compact/pay-later car when gear, early starts, suburban sites, groceries, or confirmed parking make control more valuable.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Local transport decisions for work trips, conferences, clinic trainings, and car-based leisure weekends.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: Ask for extra specifics when materials are bulky, temperature-sensitive, or need overnight security.
recovered_habits.default_action: Send a concise question list to the host or conference office and let the answers determine flights, hotel, rental, and return timing.

evidence.quote: Add parking and entrance details too. Raleigh clinics can be weird about loading zones.
Add whether I need to bring mats or if they have tables. That affects bag size.
Can you list what we still need from the host? I don't want to book blind.
Can you draft that as a concise email? I don’t want it to sound high-maintenance.
What exactly should I ask the host before we book?
Add whether the storage is climate-controlled. Some of the sample materials shouldn't sit in a car if it's warm.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: Once access, storage, and timing are confirmed, proceed with the practical travel stack; if answers remain vague, choose safer transport/hotel/return buffers or do not book.
recovered_habits.name: Gate work-trip bookings on host logistics for access, storage, equipment, and entrances
recovered_habits.preference_value: Before committing to clinic or conference travel, require concrete host answers on room access, entry points, parking/loading, storage, equipment/AV, teardown or release time, and contact procedures.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Work trips involving teaching, demo gear, lab materials, conference presentations, or hospital/clinic buildings.

recovered_habits.boundary_condition: If flight, drive, rental pickup, badge, or setup timing slips, skip groceries and use delivery, hotel market, or next-day shopping.
recovered_habits.default_action: Add an explicit food note: pack snacks, use the mini-fridge, and make any grocery stop small and conditional.

evidence.quote: Great. Add a food note. We're not going to hunt for dinner at 10 p.m.
And food? I'm too late Thursday to improvise.
Good. What about food? I was thinking groceries, but not if it risks the check.
Put groceries in only if Friday is on time. The room setup is still confirmed, right?
I don't want to start the weekend with a grocery scramble. What does Thursday look like now?
Now give me the Friday drive plan from Tampa. I want the grocery stop before check-in, but not a giant errand.

recovered_habits.exception_condition: On low-pressure leisure drives, do a small grocery stop before check-in if it avoids hovering and does not become a giant errand.
recovered_habits.name: Keep arrival food and groceries simple and conditional
recovered_habits.preference_value: Do not improvise late meals or squeeze in groceries when timing is tight; plan simple food around the room fridge/coffee, packed snacks, delivery, or a brief grocery stop only if travel is on time.
recovered_habits.scope_condition: Trips with late arrivals, early clinic starts, first-night setup, road trips, or partner recovery weekends.
